info.title: Paave API
info.description:
The Authentication domain covers OTP, login, and token lifecycle operations via identity-java, documented by the [identity service](../services/identity.md), with endpoint-level contracts grouped under the Authentication Scalar tag group. Signup account creation crosses into the Users Scalar tag group (see [users.md](users.md)).

## Signup and Login Flow

A client requests an OTP with an email address and transaction type `REGISTER`. The identity service generates a time-limited OTP and delivers it to the provided email address. The client submits the OTP value to the verify endpoint, which returns a short-lived key token on success. This key token is the credential for account creation through the Users endpoint. On success the Paave account is active; no further verification step is needed for Paave account creation.

Signup calls are public; no JWT is available yet.

| Step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request signup OTP | [`POST /api/v1/auth/otp`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/otp) | public | Body `id` (email), `idType=EMAIL`, `txType=REGISTER` | `otpId` (UUID), `expiredTime` |
| Verify signup OTP | [`POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/otp/verify) | public | Body `otpId`, `otpValue` | `keyToken` (JWT OTP key), `expiredTime` |
| Create Paave user | [`POST /api/v1/users`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users) | public | Body `registeredUsername`, `email`, `password`, `fullname`, `otpKey` | `userId` (number); **no tokens returned on signup** |

> **Verified 2026-05-05:** [`POST /api/v1/users`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users) returns `{ userId: number }` only. Tokens are not issued at signup. The client must separately call a login endpoint to obtain tokens.

Returning users can authenticate through the unified login route or the canonical password-login route. Password login validates the user credential and issues an access token plus refresh token. The two-factor login path is active as a two-step local flow: password validation returns an OTP challenge and partial token, then OTP verification completes the login challenge.

> **Test harness only — not part of production design.** Local integration tests use `OTP_CONSTANT_ENABLED=true` and `CONSTANT_OTP=123456` for deterministic OTP verification. These environment variables MUST NOT be set in any production or staging deployment.

> **Auth header format (verified 2026-05-05):** All protected endpoints require `Authorization: jwt <token>` — **not** `Bearer <token>`. The `Bearer` prefix causes 401 UNAUTHORIZED.

| Step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unified login | [`POST /api/v1/auth/login`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/login) | public | JSON body: `grant_type=password`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `username`, `password`; or `grant_type=client_credentials` with `client_id`, `client_secret`; or `grant_type=demo`. **Content-Type: application/json (not form-encoded).** | `{ accessToken, refreshToken, userInfo, userData, accExpiredTime, refExpiredTime }` |
| Password login | [`POST /api/v1/auth/login/password`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/login/password) | public | JSON body: `username`, `password` | `{ accessToken, refreshToken, userInfo, userData, accExpiredTime, refExpiredTime }` |
| Start 2FA login | [`POST /api/v1/auth/login/2fa`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/login/2fa) | public | JSON body: `username`, `password` | `{ accessToken (partial/OTP-key JWT), otpIndex (UUID), registerMobileOtp, accExpiredTime }` |
| Complete 2FA login | [`POST /api/v1/auth/login/2fa/verify-otp`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/login/2fa/verify-otp) | public | JSON body: `otp_id` (= `otpIndex` from step 1), `otp_value`, `partial_token` (= `accessToken` from step 1); optional device/platform fields | `{ accessToken, refreshToken, userInfo, userData, accExpiredTime, refExpiredTime }` |

> **2FA field names (verified 2026-05-05):** Step 1 response uses `otpIndex` (not `otpId`). Step 2 request body uses `otp_id`, `otp_value`, `partial_token` (snake_case). Step 2 now returns full access/refresh tokens.

## Token Lifecycle

The token pair (access + refresh) returned on login follows a short-TTL/long-TTL model. Access tokens carry user identity claims and authorize all API calls. Refresh tokens are long-lived and stored server-side in `identity.refresh_tokens`. Presenting a refresh token returns a new short-lived access token; the refresh token remains valid until explicitly revoked. Revocation invalidates the session.

| Step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refresh access token | [`POST /api/v1/auth/token/refresh`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/token/refresh) | public | Form-encoded: `grant_type=refresh_token`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token` | `{ accessToken, accExpiredTime }` — no refresh token rotation in response |
| Revoke session | [`POST /api/v1/auth/token/revoke`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/token/revoke) | `jwt` | Form-encoded: `refresh_token`; header: `Authorization: jwt <token>` | `{ status: true }` |

> **Verified 2026-05-05:** Token refresh response uses camelCase `accessToken` (not `access_token`). No new refresh token is returned in the refresh response. Revoke returns `{"status":true}`.

> **Legacy paths RETIRED:** `/api/v1/login`, `/api/v1/refreshToken`, `/api/v1/revokeToken`, and `/api/v1/user/accountInfo` are **not routed by the gateway** (absent from `scope_data.json`). Requests to these paths return 401 UNAUTHORIZED. Use the canonical `/api/v1/auth/*` paths instead.

## User Profile

| Step | API | Auth | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Get current user | [`GET /api/v1/users/me`](#tag/users/GET/api/v1/users/me) | `jwt` | `{ bio, email, fullname, id, username }` |

## Biometric Login

Biometric setup is an identity-owned device-binding flow. The user first confirms their password, registers a device public key (DER-encoded, base64-wrapped), verifies the OTP challenge, and then the device can authenticate by signing the biometric login payload with its private key.

> **Public key format (verified 2026-05-05):** `publicKey` must be `Base64(DER-encoded RSA public key)`, NOT Base64(PEM). Generate with: `openssl rsa -in key.pem -pubout -outform DER | base64 | tr -d '\n'`

> **Signature format (verified 2026-05-05):** The client signs `username.toUpperCase() + "|" + timestamp` (epoch milliseconds as a number). Algorithm: SHA256withRSA. Signature is base64-encoded. Timestamp must be within ±5 minutes of server time (replay prevention via Redis nonce).

| Step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Verify password before setup | [`POST /api/v1/auth/biometric/verify-password`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/biometric/verify-password) | `jwt` | JSON body: `password` | `{ success: true, message }` |
| Check device registration | [`GET /api/v1/auth/biometric/status`](#tag/authentication/GET/api/v1/auth/biometric/status) | `jwt` | Query: `deviceId` | `{ enable: boolean }` |
| Start biometric registration | [`POST /api/v1/auth/biometric/register`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/biometric/register) | `jwt` | JSON body: `password`, `publicKey` (DER base64), `deviceId` | `{ success: true, otpId, message }` |
| Complete biometric registration | [`POST /api/v1/auth/biometric/verify-otp`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/biometric/verify-otp) | `jwt` | JSON body: `otpId`, `otpValue`, `deviceId` | `{ success: true, message }` |
| Login with biometric signature | [`POST /api/v1/auth/login/biometric`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/login/biometric) | public | JSON body: `username`, `signature` (SHA256withRSA base64), `deviceId`, `timestamp` (epoch ms); optional platform/device metadata | `{ accessToken, refreshToken, userInfo, accExpiredTime, refExpiredTime }` |
| Remove biometric credential | [`POST /api/v1/auth/biometric/unregister`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/biometric/unregister) | `jwt` | JSON body: `deviceId` | `{ success: true, message }` |

> **Biometric client fix (2026-05-05):** `BiometricLoginService` previously used `findByName("mobile")` which returned `NO_ACTIVE_CLIENT` because no `mobile`-named client is seeded. Fixed to use `findByClientId("paave-ai")` (same as password-grant flow).

## Password Reset

Password reset is active when backed by a verified OTP key for transaction type `RESET_PASSWORD`. The local contract path requests a reset OTP, verifies it with the constant OTP bootstrap, and submits the resulting key token with the new password.

| Step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request reset OTP | [`POST /api/v1/auth/otp`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/otp) | public | JSON body: `id` (email), `idType=EMAIL`, `txType=RESET_PASSWORD` | `{ otpId, expiredTime }` |
| Verify reset OTP | [`POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/otp/verify) | public | JSON body: `otpId`, `otpValue` | `{ keyToken, expiredTime }` |
| Set new password | [`POST /api/v1/auth/password/reset`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/password/reset) | public | JSON body: `username`, `newPassword`, `otpKey` | `{ status: true }` |

## Local Integration Notes

### Blocked-Word Validation Applies to Fullname

The `validateName` guard on account creation applies to **both** `registeredUsername` and `fullname`. The default blocked-word list includes common test strings such as `test`. Supplying a fullname like `"E2E Test User"` returns `INVALID_PARAMETER`. Use a fullname with no blocked terms, e.g. `"Integration User"`.

### Identity Auth Config Bootstrap (Fresh Local DB)

> **Test harness only — not part of production design.** The `seedIdentityAuthConfig` helper and the Kafka consumer warmup workaround below describe local-stack QA setup; production deployment uses admin-ts Flyway migrations and a normal Kafka cluster.

`identity.clients` and `identity.login_methods` are Kafka-synced replicas populated by admin-ts when client or login-method config is published via the `vn.admin.client.update.v1` topic. On a freshly reset local DB both tables are empty and all password-grant logins return:

```
INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR: Default client 'paave-ai' not found in identity.clients.
Ensure admin-ts has published initial auth config via the vn.admin.client.update.v1 Kafka topic.
```

Because [`POST /api/v1/admin/clients`](#tag/administration/POST/api/v1/admin/clients) requires a JWT (which requires a working client), this is a circular bootstrap dependency. The test harness provides a seed helper for this exact situation:

```typescript
// paave-qa/src/lib/db/identity.ts
await seedIdentityAuthConfig("paave-ai", "HMwi84yILInRJYXhUTPGkFqB9UM1mhCsd2F");
```

This is a `@seeded-data` prerequisite step. Call it in `beforeAll` before any test that exercises password-grant login on a fresh local stack. The helper is idempotent — safe to call on subsequent runs.

**Admin-side note:** the corresponding admin.clients row is populated by admin-ts Flyway migration. If admin-ts fails to start or Kafka is down, the replica in identity never receives the event. Fix: ensure admin-ts starts cleanly before running auth suites.

### Kafka Consumer Warmup Delay

After identity-java restarts, the Kafka consumer takes approximately 26–30 seconds to warm up. Requests during this window time out at the gateway's 20-second limit. Wait for at least one successful OTP request before running login/2FA tests after a service restart.

## Provider-Gated Auth Gaps

Organization login is blocked in local Auth+Users coverage because it verifies an external organization token through the NHSV account-info path. Covering the success path requires a deterministic organization-token fixture or an approved adapter stub. Linked-account login is covered only on the local fast path where identity has an active linked-account row with unexpired broker tokens; real NHSV exchange remains part of the linked-account flow gap documented in [users.md](users.md).

| Flow | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linked-account login | [`POST /api/v1/auth/login/link-accounts`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/login/link-accounts) | `jwt` | JSON body: `partnerId` (numeric Long; partner 1 = NHSV) | Tokens scoped to the linked account |
| Organization login | [`POST /api/v1/auth/login/organization`](#tag/authentication/POST/api/v1/auth/login/organization) | public | Body `organizationId`; plus `registeredUsername`/`password` or `orgLoginToken` depending on organization mode | Organization-scoped tokens |

The Users domain covers profile management, email verification, linked-account management, password lifecycle, account deletion initiation, and partner/organization lookup surfaces owned by the [identity service](../services/identity.md), with endpoint-level contracts grouped under the Users Scalar tag group.

## Profile and Account Management

After account creation via the Authentication flow, the Users domain manages the ongoing identity lifecycle. A user fetches their profile through the current-user endpoint, updates username, full name, email, and biography through authenticated update routes, and can confirm their password for sensitive user actions. Email change uses OTP-backed confirmation and stays in identity-owned state.

| Flow step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Check username/email availability | [`POST /api/v1/users/availability-checks`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/availability-checks) | JWT | Body `type`, `value` | `available` boolean |
| Search users | [`GET /api/v1/users`](#tag/users/GET/api/v1/users) | JWT | Optional query `username`, `name`, `pageNumber`, `pageSize` | Paginated user results |
| Fetch current profile | [`GET /api/v1/users/me`](#tag/users/GET/api/v1/users/me) | JWT | none | `userId`, `username`, `fullName`, `email`, `bio`, `accountLinked` |
| Update biography | [`PUT /api/v1/users/me/bio`](#tag/users/PUT/api/v1/users/me/bio) | JWT | Body `bio` | Boolean update result |
| Update email | [`PUT /api/v1/users/me/email`](#tag/users/PUT/api/v1/users/me/email) | JWT | Body `email`, verified `otpKey` | Boolean update result |
| Update full name | [`PUT /api/v1/users/me/full-name`](#tag/users/PUT/api/v1/users/me/full-name) | JWT | Body `fullname` | Boolean update result |
| Update username | [`PUT /api/v1/users/me/username`](#tag/users/PUT/api/v1/users/me/username) | JWT | Body `username`, optional `otpKey` | Boolean update result |
| Confirm account | [`POST /api/v1/users/me/confirmation`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/me/confirmation) | JWT | Body `password` | Boolean confirmation result |
| Submit feedback | [`POST /api/v1/users/me/feedbacks`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/me/feedbacks) | JWT | Body `deviceId`, `appVersion`, optional `message`, `rating` | Boolean submit result |
| Disable/suspend own account | [`PUT /api/v1/users/me/status`](#tag/users/PUT/api/v1/users/me/status) | JWT | Body `reason` | Boolean status update result |

## Password Lifecycle

Paave supports checking whether a password exists, setting an initial password for accounts created without one, and changing an existing password. Contract coverage uses isolated `bootstrapTestUser()` accounts and identity-owned setup helpers when a test must place the account in the "no password available" lifecycle state. Password reset itself is documented in the Authentication flow because the public reset route is tagged Authentication.

| Flow step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Check password availability | [`GET /api/v1/users/me/password/availability`](#tag/users/GET/api/v1/users/me/password/availability) | JWT | none | `available` boolean |
| Set initial password | [`POST /api/v1/users/me/password/initial`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/me/password/initial) | JWT | Body `password` | Boolean create result |
| Change password | [`POST /api/v1/users/me/password`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/me/password) | JWT | Body `oldPassword`, `newPassword` | Boolean change result |

## Linked Account Management

Live trading requires linking a brokerage account through the NHSV broker. The linked-account sub-resource under Users records the binding state from local draft to verified draft to active linked account. Listing linked accounts, creating a local draft, promoting a verified local draft, updating partner username, toggling leaderboard visibility, resolving users by partner account, and unlinking by partner are locally covered with identity-owned fixtures.

The real NHSV OTP exchange remains provider-gated: confirmation, approval, outbound partner OTP notification, and inbound partner OTP verification require adapter-broker-nhsv and a safe broker account path. Unlinking is only supported by `partnerId`; the identity request DTO binds `partnerId`, so an account-ID-keyed unlink route is intentionally not exposed.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Confirm broker link | [`POST /api/v1/users/me/link-accounts/confirmation`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/me/link-accounts/confirmation) | JWT | Body `sessionId`, `partnerPassword` | Boolean confirmation result |
| Create final linked account | [`POST /api/v1/users/me/link-accounts`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/me/link-accounts) | JWT | Body `sessionId`, `otp` | `201`, link `status`, `partnerAccountNumber` |

| Change linked username | [`POST /api/v1/users/me/link-accounts/username`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/me/link-accounts/username) | JWT | Body `partnerId`, `newUsername` | Boolean update result |
| Update leaderboard visibility | [`PUT /api/v1/users/me/link-accounts/leaderboard/settings`](#tag/users/PUT/api/v1/users/me/link-accounts/leaderboard/settings) | JWT | Body `partnerId`, `optBoard`, optional `subAccount` | Boolean update result |
| Send OTP to partner | [`POST /api/v1/users/me/partner-otp-notifications`](#tag/users/POST/api/v1/users/me/partner-otp-notifications) | JWT | Body `sessionId`, `otp` | Boolean notification result |

## Account Deletion

Account deletion initiation and resend-notification are covered as local identity contracts. Completing deletion is blocked in this slice because it anonymizes the user and calls cross-service status/ranking side effects. Covering completion requires an isolated deletion harness with deterministic user-status and virtual/live ranking sinks.

| Flow step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |

The Virtual Trading domain covers simulated trading, contests, and settlement state via trading-virtual-java, documented by the [trading-virtual service](../services/trading-virtual.md), with endpoint-level contracts grouped under the Virtual Trading Scalar tag group.

## Virtual Order Lifecycle

A new user creates a virtual trading account. The account is funded with a virtual balance on creation. The user places buy and sell orders against HOSE, HNX, and UPCoM symbols. Orders enter `PENDING` state when accepted by the order core; the exchange simulator then accepts the order into its matching cache and transitions it to `RECEIVED`. When the matching engine finds a counterpart the order moves to `FILLED_ALL`; buy-side cash is deducted at match time, sell-side securities are deducted at match time, and sell-side cash remains pending until settlement. Active orders are in `{PENDING, RECEIVED}`; an order in either state can be canceled or expired.

All virtual trading APIs require JWT authentication.

## P&L and Settlement

Profit-and-loss figures are computed from the filled order set and are available via the P&L and daily-P&L endpoints. Sellable quantity and purchasable amount are derived from the current portfolio and exposed as dedicated read endpoints to inform the order form. The virtual settlement job is a T+2 settlement-date model, but VN equity availability should be tested as before the afternoon session on T+2, i.e. T+1.5 availability. Test flows use `12:30 Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` on the settlement date as the deterministic availability point. T+2 cash settlement credits the proceeds from sell-side fills. T+2 quantity settlement makes buy-side filled quantities available to sell. Buy-side cash deduction occurs at match time, not at settlement.

| Flow step | API | Caller input | Expected output |

### Full Cycle Verification Flow

> **QA harness notes — not part of the design contract.** The table below documents the test-only harness used to drive a full buy → match → settle → sell cycle without waiting for real market quotes or T+2 settlement dates. The `MATCH_BUY_SIDE` / `MATCH_SELL_SIDE` DB helpers and the settlement-date backdating mutations are reserved for the integration test harness only. Production code must never invoke them.

Full virtual-trading QA must cover both sides of the order cycle. Because a local test run may not receive the market quote that would match an order, and because settlement would otherwise require waiting for the settlement date, the QA harness may mutate only `trading_virtual` rows after API placement.

| Phase | API or DB action | Required assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before buy | [`GET /api/v1/virtual/equity/accounts/buyable`](#tag/virtual-trading/GET/api/v1/virtual/equity/accounts/buyable); DB read `balances` and `positions` | Capture cash, buying power, quantity, and sellable baseline. |
| Place buy | [`POST /api/v1/virtual/equity/orders`](#tag/virtual-trading/POST/api/v1/virtual/equity/orders) with `orderCommand=LO`, `action=BUY` | Order exists in `PENDING` or `RECEIVED`; `buying_power` decreased by reserved `trading_value + fee`; `balance` unchanged. |
| Check unmatched order | [`GET /api/v1/virtual/equity/orders/history`](#tag/virtual-trading/GET/api/v1/virtual/equity/orders/history) | Order is visible before match mutation. |
| Match buy | DB helper calls `trading_virtual.MATCH_BUY_SIDE(orderId, quantity, price, quoteTime)` | Order becomes `FILLED_ALL`; `balance` decreases by matched `trading_value + fee`; `positions.quantity` increases; `positions.sellable` unchanged. |
| Settle buy | DB helper backdates the order to the T-2 business date, then applies settlement mutation | Order becomes `SETTLEMENT`; `positions.sellable` increases by matched quantity. |
| Before sell | [`GET /api/v1/virtual/equity/accounts/sellable`](#tag/virtual-trading/GET/api/v1/virtual/equity/accounts/sellable); DB read `balances` and `positions` | Sellable quantity is at least the sell quantity; cash baseline is captured. |
| Place sell | [`POST /api/v1/virtual/equity/orders`](#tag/virtual-trading/POST/api/v1/virtual/equity/orders) with `orderCommand=LO`, `action=SELL` | Order exists in `PENDING` or `RECEIVED`; `positions.sellable` decreases by order quantity; cash unchanged. |
| Match sell | DB helper calls `trading_virtual.MATCH_SELL_SIDE(orderId, quantity, price, quoteTime)` | Order becomes `FILLED_ALL`; `positions.quantity` decreases; cash remains unchanged. |
| Settle sell | DB helper backdates the order to the T-2 business date, then applies settlement mutation | Order becomes `SETTLEMENT`; `balances.balance` and `balances.buying_power` increase by `trading_value - fee - selling_tax`. |
| Dividend event | Insert a corporate-event fixture, insert one `event_dividends` receivable, settle it through the DB helper, then call [`GET /api/v1/virtual/equity/event/by-stock`](#tag/virtual-trading/GET/api/v1/virtual/equity/event/by-stock) and `profit-loss` | Cash dividend increases `balance` and `buying_power`; stock dividend increases `positions.sellable`; API event/read endpoints remain healthy. |

## Channel Binding and Message Flow

The Messenger domain bridges Paave user accounts to external chat channels (Zalo, Telegram) through a magic-link token flow. A Paave user requests a link token via the Messenger REST endpoints served by the gateway; the token is persisted in the [identity service](../services/identity.md) with a short TTL and a one-time-use constraint. The user sends the token as a message to the Paave channel bot; the [claw-channel service](../services/claw-channel.md) calls the `consume_link_token_by_code` Kafka-RPC on the [identity service](../services/identity.md); identity validates the token, atomically marks it consumed, writes the binding to `messenger_bindings`, and publishes the binding event via the transactional outbox.

Messenger REST routes require JWT authentication because they bind an already-authenticated Paave web session to a channel identity.

| Flow | API | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flow 2, web-initiated token mint | `POST /api/v1/link-tokens` | Header `Idempotency-Key`; body `channel` | `201`, one-time cleartext `code`, `expiresAt` |
| Flow 1, bot-initiated confirm-screen context | `GET /api/v1/link-tokens/by-handle/{opaque}/context` | Path `opaque` handle from `?t=<opaque>` | `state`, `expiresAt`, `channel`, masked channel user ID, `mintedAt` |
| Flow 1, consume handle on web confirm | `POST /api/v1/link-tokens/by-handle/{opaque}/consume` | Header `Idempotency-Key`; path `opaque` | `paaveUserId`, `bindingId`, `channel`, masked channel user ID |

## Message Receive and LLM Dispatch

Once bound, inbound messages from the chat channel arrive at the [claw-channel service](../services/claw-channel.md) as webhook events. The channel service persists the message, publishes it to the internal Kafka topic, and the [claw-agent service](../services/claw-agent.md) claims the turn for LLM processing. The agent composes a response using the configured LLM provider, records the turn audit, and dispatches the reply outbound via claw-channel. This flow requires the ai service group to be running. The Messenger Scalar tag group covers the three REST endpoints involved in the link-token lifecycle.

| Flow step | API / internal call | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| User sends `/login` in bot | `claw-channel -> identity` Kafka RPC `mint_link_token_bot_initiated` | Channel, channel user ID, idempotency key | Opaque handle and expiry; channel replies with a web confirm URL |
| Web confirm page peeks handle | `GET /api/v1/link-tokens/by-handle/{opaque}/context` | Authenticated Paave JWT and opaque handle | Context for the confirm UI |
| Web confirm page consumes handle | `POST /api/v1/link-tokens/by-handle/{opaque}/consume` | Authenticated Paave JWT, opaque handle, `Idempotency-Key` | Binding row identity |
| User sends `/login <code>` in bot | `claw-channel -> identity` Kafka RPC `peek_link_token_by_code` then `consume_link_token_by_code` | Cleartext code from Flow 2, channel identity | Binding success/failure reply in the channel |

The Claw domain covers webhook ingest, slash commands, LLM turn orchestration, and outbound dispatch across the [claw-channel service](../services/claw-channel.md) and [claw-agent service](../services/claw-agent.md); it requires the `ai` group and maps to the Claw Scalar tag group.

## Webhook Ingest and LLM Turn

The Claw domain covers the internal webhook and slash-command surface that [claw-channel](../services/claw-channel.md) exposes to external channel providers. Inbound webhook events from Zalo and Telegram are authenticated, normalized, and persisted as message-history rows. Slash commands are dispatched to their handlers synchronously; freeform messages are routed to the [claw-agent service](../services/claw-agent.md) for LLM processing.

The Claw Scalar tag has the public channel webhook and a health route. The webhook itself is public at the HTTP-auth layer, but channel-specific signatures are mandatory before any body parsing or persistence.

| Flow step | API | Auth | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Receive channel webhook | `POST /webhook/claw/{channel}` | public HTTP plus provider signature | Path `channel`; raw Telegram/Zalo webhook payload; provider signature header such as Telegram secret token or Zalo HMAC | `200` after accepted dispatch; `401` on signature failure; no Paave JWT |
| Check claw-channel health | `GET /health` | public | none | Service health response |
| Bot-initiated login command | `POST /webhook/claw/{channel}` carrying `/login` | provider signature | Channel payload with `/login` command | Transport reply containing confirm link; internal identity RPC mints opaque handle |
| Web-code login command | `POST /webhook/claw/{channel}` carrying `/login <code>` | provider signature | Channel payload with code | Transport reply with binding result; code is redacted before persistence |
| Freeform message | `POST /webhook/claw/{channel}` | provider signature | Channel payload with text/media metadata | Message history row plus `vn.claw.message.inbound.v1` outbox event for claw-agent |

## Outbound Dispatch

After the LLM turn completes, [claw-agent](../services/claw-agent.md) publishes the reply to the `vn.claw.message.outbound.v1` Kafka topic. The [claw-channel service](../services/claw-channel.md) consumes from that topic, atomically inserts a claim row in `claw.outbound_claims` together with a `message_history` dispatch event, invokes the channel SDK, and transitions the claim to a terminal state (`delivered`, `inconclusive`, or `failed_retrying`). Claims that stall in `claimed` state are recovered by a periodic sweep and marked `inconclusive` for ops review. This flow requires the `ai` service group. The Claw Scalar tag group covers the two inbound webhook endpoints.

| Flow step | API / internal topic | Caller input | Expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Agent replies | `vn.claw.message.outbound.v1` | `ClawMessageOutbound` with channel, channel user, nullable `paaveUserId`, message body | claw-channel claim row and outbound dispatch attempt |
| Alert/briefing dispatch | `vn.insights.notification.messenger.dispatch.v1` | Alert or briefing envelope from insights | claw-channel dispatch using local binding projection |
| Binding fence for transport replies | `claw-channel -> identity` Kafka RPC `lookup_binding` | `paaveUserId`, channel, channel user ID | Continue dispatch on binding match; mark `inconclusive` on timeout |
| Channel SDK call | Provider SDK/API | Redacted outbound body and provider destination | Claim state `delivered`, `failed_retrying`, `terminal`, `binding_revoked`, or `inconclusive` |
